newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket launches two satellites for Asia.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket launches two satellites for Asia.

text.p: Western Europe's 95th Ariane rocket blasted off from French Guiana on Wednesday carrying two satellites to service Asia.
The Ariane-4 rocket lifted off at 8:08 p.m/7:08 p.m. EST (2308 GMT) from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
Twenty minutes later, launch space officials said the Thaicom 3 satellite separated from the Ariane rocket.
Thaicom 3 will provide voice, data and video services throughout Asia for the Bangkok-based Shinawatra Satellite Company. It was built by France's Aerospatiale.

Four minutes later the BSAT-1a satellite, built by Los Angeles-based Hughes Space & Communications was released. It will be used for direct television broadcasting over Japan for Tokyo-based Broadcasting Satellite System (B-SAT).
Wednesday's mission was the third of 12 Ariane rocket launches planned for this year by the Paris-based Ariane space company.
